instruction: What is the Delimited Text driver and what does it do?
output: The Delimited Text driver lets you use delimited text files (CSV) to synchronize data between the Identity Vault and applications. Essentially, it allows you to transfer data from the Identity Vault to any system that can consume delimited text files, or transfer data to the Identity Vault from any system that can generate delimited text files.

instruction: Can the Delimited Text driver work with file formats other than CSV?
output: Yes, the Delimited Text driver can also be modified to consume XML files in addition to delimited text files (CSV).

instruction: In which directions can the Delimited Text driver synchronize data?
output: The Delimited Text driver can synchronize data bidirectionally: it can transfer data from the Identity Vault to any system that can consume delimited text files, and it can also transfer data to the Identity Vault from any system that can generate delimited text files.

instruction: How does the Delimited Text driver control data flow between the Identity Vault and delimited text files?
output: The Delimited Text driver uses the Publisher channel, the Subscriber channel, and policies to control data flow between the Identity Vault and delimited text files. The Publisher channel reads information from input text files on the local file system and submits it to the Identity Vault via the Identity Manager engine. The Subscriber channel watches for additions and modifications to Identity Vault objects and creates output files on the local file system that reflect those changes. Policies control the data synchronization between the driver and the Identity Vault.

instruction: What is the purpose of the Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver?
output: The Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver reads information from input text files on the local file system and submits that information to the Identity Vault via the Identity Manager engine. By default, it checks the input directory every 10 seconds, processes any files that have a .csv extension, changes the .csv extensions of processed files to .bak, and cycles through this process until the driver is stopped.

instruction: What does the Subscriber channel do in the Delimited Text driver?
output: The Subscriber channel in the Delimited Text driver watches for additions and modifications to Identity Vault objects and creates output files on the local file system that reflect those changes. By default, the Subscriber channel keeps an output file open until either 200 transactions have been logged or 30 seconds have elapsed. When either of these thresholds is reached, the output file is saved with a number.csv filename and a new output file is opened.

instruction: What are the default processing intervals and file extension behavior for the Delimited Text driver's Publisher channel?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Publisher channel has the following default behavior: it checks the input directory every 10 seconds, processes any files that have a .csv extension, and changes the .csv extensions of processed files to .bak. This cycle continues until the driver is stopped.

instruction: What are the default thresholds that trigger file closure in the Subscriber channel of the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver's Subscriber channel, the default thresholds for closing an output file are: either 200 transactions have been logged or 30 seconds have elapsed, whichever occurs first. When either threshold is reached, the output file is saved with a number.csv filename and a new output file is opened.

instruction: Which Identity Vault User properties are mapped to application attributes by the Schema Map policy in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Schema Map policy maps Identity Vault User properties to application attributes as follows: Surname > LastName, Given Name > FirstName, Title > Title, Internet EMail Address > Email, Telephone Number > WorkPhone, Facsimile Telephone Number > Fax, mobile > WirelessPhone, and Description > Description. The application attributes correspond to the sequence of values in the file or to the attributes associated with unnamed XDS <field> elements if present.

instruction: What does the Input Transform policy do in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Input Transform policy is configured on the driver object. If the input document is an XML document, no transformations are made. If the document is a delimited text file, each record is transformed into an XDS Add element for User objects with attributes defined by the schema map. Associations are defined by the value of the user's e-mail attribute.

instruction: What is the function of the Output Transform policy in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Output Transform policy is configured on the driver object. It specifies that a comma is used as the delimiter character for output files and that the file format is comma-separated value (CSV) format. This policy transforms the XDS document into CSV format and submits it to the driver shim.

instruction: What requirements does the Create policy specify for creating a User in the Identity Vault using the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Create policy is configured on the Publisher channel and specifies that in order for a User to be created in an Identity Vault, the Given Name and Internet EMail Address attributes must be defined. The user CN is formed by concatenating the values of first name and last name.

instruction: How does the Matching policy determine if a user in the Identity Vault is the same as a user specified in the input file for the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Matching policy is configured on the Publisher channel and specifies that a user in an Identity Vault is the same user specified in the input file when the value of Internet Email Address is the same in both places. If there is a match, only changed attributes are updated in the Identity Vault.

instruction: What container placement does the Placement policy specify for new users in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Placement policy is configured on the Publisher channel and specifies that a new user is placed in the Users or Active container and named with the CN created by the Input Transform rule. You need to create a Users\Active container at the root of your tree before you start the driver.

instruction: What transformation does the Event Transform policy perform in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the Event Transform policy is configured on the Subscriber channel. If an Identity Vault reports a Modify or Sync event, those events are changed to an instance element that can be used to create a complete output record.

instruction: Which two file types does the Delimited Text driver currently support?
output: The Delimited Text driver currently supports two types of files: Comma-Separated Values (CSV) files and XML files in XDS format.

instruction: What are Comma-Separated Values files and how are they structured in the context of the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, Comma-separated value (CSV) files are text files that contain data divided into fields and records. Fields are delimited by commas, and records are delimited by a hard return. If a comma or hard return is needed within the value of a particular field, the entire field value should be enclosed in quotes. Because the meaning of each field in a CSV file is derived from its position, each record should have the same number of fields. Field values can be left blank, but each record should have the same number of delimiter characters.

instruction: What is the XDS format supported by the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the XDS format is the defined NetIQ subset of possible XML formats. This is the initial format for data coming from an Identity Vault. By modifying default rules and changing the style sheets, the Delimited Text driver can be configured to work with any XML format.

instruction: If only one-way data flow is required in the Delimited Text driver, what should be done with the unused channel?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, when only one-way data flow is required, only a Publisher or Subscriber channel is used depending on the direction needed. The other channel should be disabled.

instruction: Provide a concise summary of how the Delimited Text driver works.
output: The Delimited Text driver synchronizes data between the Identity Vault and delimited text files using two channels and policies. The Publisher channel reads input text files (by default, .csv files checked every 10 seconds) and submits data to the Identity Vault. The Subscriber channel monitors Identity Vault changes and creates output files (closed after 200 transactions or 30 seconds). Seven preconfigured policies control synchronization: Schema Map (maps User properties to attributes), Input Transform (converts CSV to XDS Add elements), Output Transform (converts XDS to CSV), Create (requires Given Name and Email for user creation), Matching (matches users by Internet Email Address), Placement (places new users in Users\Active container), and Event Transform (converts Modify/Sync events to instance elements). The driver supports CSV files and XML files in XDS format. Many configurations use only one channel for one-way synchronization.

instruction: What Java interfaces are provided by the Delimited Text driver and what is their purpose?
output: The Delimited Text driver includes four Java interfaces that enable you to add extensions. These enhancements to the driver are optional and require Java programming to implement custom file processing capabilities.

instruction: Are the Java interfaces in the Delimited Text driver required or optional?
output: The Java interfaces in the Delimited Text driver are optional enhancements. You can use the driver without implementing these interfaces, but they are available if you need to customize file processing through Java programming.

instruction: What programming language is required to create extensions using the Delimited Text driver interfaces?
output: Java programming is required to create extensions using the Delimited Text driver interfaces. These enhancements enable customization of file processing in the driver.

instruction: Summarize the key extensibility features available in the Delimited Text driver.
output: The Delimited Text driver provides four Java interfaces that allow developers to optionally extend and customize the driver's file processing capabilities through Java programming. These extensions are not mandatory but offer enhanced functionality for organizations with specific customization needs.

instruction: Where can the Delimited Text driver run in a NetIQ Identity Manager deployment?
output: The Delimited Text driver can run in two locations: directly on the Identity Manager server, or on another server using the Remote Loader.

instruction: How does password synchronization work in the Delimited Text driver?
output: The Delimited Text driver does not have automatic password synchronization. Instead, password synchronization must be implemented as attribute synchronization. You must decide which attribute will hold the password value and then synchronize that attribute. The driver includes policies to handle this password synchronization, but it functions as standard attribute synchronization rather than dedicated password synchronization.

instruction: Does the Delimited Text driver support automatic password synchronization?
output: No, the Delimited Text driver does not support automatic password synchronization. You must manually configure password synchronization by selecting an attribute to hold the password and synchronizing that attribute. Any password synchronization for the Delimited Text driver is implemented as attribute synchronization.

instruction: What is the Remote Loader option for the Delimited Text driver?
output: The Remote Loader is a deployment option for the Delimited Text driver that allows the driver to run on a server other than the Identity Manager server. This provides flexibility in distributed architectures where the driver needs to access delimited text files on remote systems.

instruction: What are the key features of the Delimited Text driver in NetIQ Identity Manager?
output: The Delimited Text driver has two key features: (1) Flexible deployment - it can run either locally on the Identity Manager server or remotely on another server using the Remote Loader, and (2) Password synchronization support - while the driver includes policies for handling passwords, it does not provide automatic password synchronization. Instead, passwords must be synchronized as regular attributes, where you select which attribute holds the password value and configure synchronization for that attribute.

instruction: What is installed by default when the Delimited Text driver files are installed on the Identity Manager server?
output: When the Delimited Text driver files are installed by default on the Identity Manager server, the installation program performs the following actions: extends the Identity Vault's schema, installs both the driver shim, and installs the driver configuration files. However, the installation does NOT create the driver in the Identity Vault or upgrade an existing driver's configuration.

instruction: Why must the input directory for the Delimited Text driver be located on the same server as the driver?
output: Unless you extend the Delimited Text driver's functionality using Java interfaces, the driver is only capable of reading input text files from the local file system of the server where the driver is running. This limitation means that the input directory must be located on the same server as the driver to enable file reading operations.

instruction: What are the three options for handling input directory location with the Delimited Text driver?
output:
The three options for handling input directory location with the Delimited Text driver are:

1. If your input directory can be located on the Identity Manager server and the Delimited Text driver files are already installed on the server, you can skip driver file installation and proceed with creating a new driver object.

2. If your input directory can be located on the Identity Manager server but the driver files are not already installed, install the files using the instructions in the NetIQ Identity Manager Setup Guide for Linux or Windows.

3. If your input directory cannot be located on the Identity Manager server, install the Remote Loader (required to run the driver on a non-Identity Manager server) and the driver files on the server where the input directory resides.

instruction: How do you enable the Delimited Text driver to read input files from a server other than the Identity Manager server?
output: To enable the Delimited Text driver to read input files from a server other than the Identity Manager server, you must install the Remote Loader and the Delimited Text driver files on the server where the input directory resides. The Remote Loader is required to run the driver on a non-Identity Manager server.

instruction: In the Delimited Text driver, what functionality requires extending the driver with Java interfaces?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, extending the driver's functionality with Java interfaces is required to enable the driver to read input text files from locations other than the local file system of the server where the driver is running. Without this extension, the driver can only read files from the local file system.

instruction: Summarize the key considerations for installing the Delimited Text driver files in an Identity Manager environment.
output: The Delimited Text driver files are installed by default on the Identity Manager server along with the Identity Manager engine, extending the Identity Vault schema and installing the driver shim and configuration files. The driver can only read input text files from the local file system unless extended with Java interfaces. Depending on where your input directory is located, you have three options: proceed directly to driver object creation if files are already installed on the Identity Manager server, install driver files on the Identity Manager server if not already present, or install the Remote Loader and driver files on a separate server where the input directory resides if it cannot be located on the Identity Manager server.

instruction: What is the general process for creating a new driver object in the Identity Vault for the Delimited Text driver?
output: For the Delimited Text driver, you create the driver object in the Identity Vault by installing the driver packages and then modifying the driver configuration to suit your environment. The process involves preparing data locations, creating the driver object in Designer, activating the driver object, and optionally adding packages to an existing driver.

instruction: What are the main steps involved in setting up the Delimited Text driver object?
output:
To set up the Delimited Text driver object, follow these main steps:
1. Prepare data locations
2. Create the driver object in Designer
3. Activate the driver object
4. Add packages to an existing driver (if needed)

instruction: Summarize the key components involved in creating a new Delimited Text driver object.
output: Creating a new Delimited Text driver object involves four key components: preparing the necessary data locations, creating the driver object using Designer, activating the driver object to make it operational, and optionally adding packages to an existing driver for additional functionality. The process requires installing driver packages and then customizing the driver configuration to match your specific environment requirements.

instruction: What are the input and output directories used for in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the input directory is where the driver looks for files to be processed into the Identity Vault. The output directory is where the driver places files to be processed by the target application.

instruction: Where must the input and output directories for the Delimited Text driver be located?
output: The input and output directories for the Delimited Text driver must be located on the same server as the driver. The directories can have any names supported by the server operating system.

instruction: How do you prepare data locations for the Delimited Text driver?
output: To prepare data locations for the Delimited Text driver, you need to make sure that the driver's input and output directories exist. The input directory is where the driver looks for files to be processed into the Identity Vault, and the output directory is where the driver places files to be processed by the target application. Both directories must be located on the same server as the driver and can have any names supported by the server operating system.

instruction: Summarize the requirements for preparing data locations in the Delimited Text driver.
output: For the Delimited Text driver, you must create input and output directories on the same server as the driver. The input directory is used for files being processed into the Identity Vault, while the output directory holds files for the target application. Directory names can be any names supported by the server operating system.

instruction: What are driver packages in the Delimited Text driver and what do they contain?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, driver packages contain the items required to create a driver, such as policies, entitlements, filters, and Schema Mapping policies. These packages are only available in Designer. The driver includes several packages: the Delimited Text Base package (required), Delimited Text Entitlements (for quick onboarding of custom entitlements and dynamic resource creation), Delimited Text Password Synchronization (with GCVs and sample policies for synchronizing passwords), and Delimited Text Managed System Information (policies that enable the driver to collect data for reports).

instruction: How do you import the current driver packages for the Delimited Text driver in Designer?
output:
To import the current driver packages for the Delimited Text driver in Designer:

1. Open Designer.
2. In the toolbar, click Help > Check for Package Updates.
3. Click OK if there are no package updates, or click OK to import the package updates.
4. In the Outline view, right-click the Package Catalog.
5. Click Import Package.
6. Select the Delimited Text packages, or click Select All to import all of the packages displayed, then click OK. By default, only the base packages are displayed. Deselect Show Base Packages Only to display all packages.
7. Click OK to import the selected packages, then click OK in the successfully imported packages message.

instruction: What are the step-by-step instructions for installing the Delimited Text driver packages in Designer?
output:
To install the Delimited Text driver packages:

1. Start Designer and open your project.
2. In the Modeler, right-click the driver set where you want to create your new driver, then select New > Driver.
3. Select Delimited Text Base from the list of base packages, then click Next.
4. Select the optional features to install (Delimited Text Entitlements, Delimited Text Password Synchronization, Delimited Text Managed System Information), then click Next.
5. Click Next.
6. (Optional) If you want the driver to synchronize passwords, select the Delimited Text Password Synchronization package, then click Next.
7. (Conditional) If not already configured, fill in User Container and Group Container on the Common Settings page, then click Next.
8. (Conditional) If not already configured, fill in User Application Provisioning Services URL and Administrator on the Common Settings Advanced Edition page, then click Next.
9. On the Install Delimited Text Base page, specify a name for the driver, then click Next.
10. Fill in Input File Path and Output File Path, then click Next.
11. (Conditional) Configure Remote Loader settings if desired, then click Next.
12. On the Driver Parameters page, fill in Field Delimiter and Field Names, then click Next.
13-15. (Conditional) Fill in Managed System Information fields if that package was installed, then click Next.
16. Review the settings and click Finish to create the driver.

instruction: What are the required Driver Parameters for the Delimited Text driver and what do they mean?
output:
The required Driver Parameters for the Delimited Text driver are:

* **Field Delimiter:** Specify the character to use to delimit field values in the input and output files. It must be one character. You can also use the tab as the delimiter field value. Tab is represented as {tab}. The default is a comma.
* **Field Names:** Specify a comma-separated list of attribute names that can be referred to in the Schema Mapping rule. The fields of the records included in your input CSV files must correspond to the order and positioning of the names in this list.

Additionally, the driver requires:
* **Input File Path:** Specify the path for the input file.
* **Output File Path:** Specify the path for the output file.

instruction: What optional packages are available for the Delimited Text driver and what does each provide?
output:
The optional packages available for the Delimited Text driver are:

* **Delimited Text Entitlements:** This package contains policies for quick onboarding of custom entitlements and dynamic resource creation. This package also contains GCVs to control the resource mapping. Select this package if you want to enable the entitlement onboarding feature for this driver. If you are enabling quick onboarding of custom entitlements functionality, ensure that you upgrade the Managed System Gateway driver version to 4.0.0.6.
* **Delimited Text Password Synchronization:** This package contains GCVs and sample policies for synchronizing passwords.
* **Delimited Text Managed System Information:** This package contains the policies that enable the driver to collect data for reports.

instruction: What Remote Loader configuration parameters are required for the Delimited Text driver?
output:
The Remote Loader configuration parameters for the Delimited Text driver are:

* **Connect to Remote Loader:** By default, the driver is configured to connect through the Remote Loader. If you want to run the driver locally, select no. Otherwise, fill in the remaining fields.
* **Host Name:** Specify the host name or IP address of the server where the driver's Remote Loader service is running.
* **Port:** Specify the port number where the Remote Loader is installed and is running for this driver. The default port number is 8090.
* **Remote Password:** Specify the Remote Loader's password, as defined on the Remote Loader. The Identity Manager server or the Remote Loader shim requires this password to authenticate to the Remote Loader.
* **Driver Password:** Specify the driver object password that is defined in the Remote Loader service. The Remote Loader requires this password to authenticate to the Identity Manager server.

instruction: How do you deploy the Delimited Text driver object to the Identity Vault?
output:
To deploy the Delimited Text driver object to the Identity Vault:

1. In the Modeler, right-click the driver icon or the driver line, then select Live > Deploy.
2. If you are not authenticated to the Identity Vault, specify Host (IP address or DNS name of the server hosting the Identity Vault), Username (DN of the user object used to authenticate), and Password, then click OK.
3. Read through the deployment summary, then click Deploy.
4. Read the successful message, then click OK.
5. Click Define Security Equivalence to assign rights to the driver. Click Add, browse to and select the object with the correct rights, then click OK twice.
6. Click Exclude Administrative Roles to exclude users that should not be synchronized. Click Add, browse to and select the user object you want to exclude, then click OK. Repeat for each object to exclude, then click OK.
7. Click OK.

instruction: What security rights does the Delimited Text driver require in the Identity Vault?
output:
For the Delimited Text driver to receive events from the Identity Vault, the driver's Security Equals DN requires the following rights:

* **Entry:** Browse rights.
* **Attributes:** Read rights.

The driver also requires rights to objects within the Identity Vault and to the input and output directories on the server. The Admin user object is most often used to supply these rights. However, you might want to create a DriversUser, for example, and assign security equivalence to that user.

instruction: What fields are required when configuring Managed System Information for the Delimited Text driver?
output:
When configuring Managed System Information for the Delimited Text driver, the following fields are required:

**System Definition:**
* **Name:** Specify a descriptive name for this Delimited Text system.
* **Description:** Specify a brief description for this Delimited Text system.
* **Location:** Specify the physical location of this Delimited Text system.
* **Vendor:** Leave the setting unchanged.
* **Version:** Specify the version of this Delimited Text system.

**Ownership:**
* **Business Owner:** Select a user object in the Identity Vault that is the business owner of the Delimited Text system. This can only be a user object, not a role, group, or container.
* **Application Owner:** Select a user object in the Identity Vault that is the application owner of the Delimited Text system. This can only be a user object, not a role, group, or container.

**Classification and Environment:**
* **Classification:** Select the classification of the Delimited Text system (Mission-Critical, Vital, Not-Critical, or Other). If you select Other, you must specify a custom classification.
* **Environment:** Select the type of environment the Delimited Text system provides (Development, Test, Staging, Production, or Other). If you select Other, you must specify a custom classification.

instruction: How do you modify driver settings for the Delimited Text driver after installation?
output:
To modify driver settings for the Delimited Text driver after installation:

1. Open your project in Designer.
2. In the Modeler, right-click the driver icon or the driver line, then select Properties.
3. The Driver Properties page displays settings divided into categories such as Driver Configuration, Engine Control Values, and Global Configuration Values (GCVs). Your first priority should be to review the Driver Parameters located on the Driver Configuration page, which let you control the format and content of the input and output files.
4. Click OK when finished.
5. Deploy the driver to the Identity Vault.

instruction: Why should you exclude administrative roles when deploying the Delimited Text driver?
output: You should exclude administrative User objects (for example, Admin and DriversUser) from synchronization when deploying the Delimited Text driver to prevent these privileged accounts from being synchronized between the Identity Vault and the connected system. This is a best practice to maintain security and prevent potential issues with administrative account management. During deployment, you can add these objects to the exclusion list by clicking Exclude Administrative Roles, then clicking Add and browsing to select each user object you want to exclude.

instruction: What is the procedure for checking and updating packages before creating a Delimited Text driver object?
output:
To verify you have the latest packages in the Package Catalog before creating a Delimited Text driver object:

1. Open Designer.
2. In the toolbar, click Help > Check for Package Updates.
3. Click OK if there are no package updates, or click OK to import the package updates.
4. In the Outline view, right-click the Package Catalog.
5. Click Import Package.
6. Select the Delimited Text packages, or click Select All to import all of the packages displayed, then click OK. (By default, only the base packages are displayed. Deselect Show Base Packages Only to display all packages.)
7. Click OK to import the selected packages, then click OK in the successfully imported packages message.

It is recommended to have the latest packages in the Package Catalog before creating a new driver object.

instruction: What is the default field delimiter in the Delimited Text driver and how can you specify a tab character?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the default field delimiter is a comma. The field delimiter specifies the character used to delimit field values in the input and output files, and it must be one character. You can also use the tab as the delimiter field value, which is represented as {tab}.

instruction: What is the purpose of the Common Settings package in the Delimited Text driver installation?
output: The Common Settings package in the Delimited Text driver installation provides default configuration values that apply to all drivers in the driver set. Specifically, it allows you to configure the User Container (where users are added if they don't already exist in the Identity Vault) and the Group Container (where groups are added if they don't already exist in the Identity Vault). The Common Settings page is only displayed during installation if the Common Settings package is a dependency. These values become the default values for all drivers in the driver set.

instruction: Summarize the key steps and considerations for creating a Delimited Text driver object in Designer.
output:
Creating a Delimited Text driver object in Designer involves several key steps:

1. **Import Current Packages:** Check for and import the latest Delimited Text driver packages from the Package Catalog, ensuring you have the most recent versions.

2. **Install Driver Packages:** Select the Delimited Text Base package (required) and choose optional packages including Entitlements, Password Synchronization, and Managed System Information based on your requirements.

3. **Configure Driver Settings:** Specify essential parameters including Input File Path, Output File Path, Field Delimiter (default is comma, or {tab} for tab), and Field Names (comma-separated list of attribute names). Optionally configure Remote Loader connection settings if running the driver remotely.

4. **Set System Information:** If using Managed System Information package, define system details including Name, Description, Location, Version, Business Owner, Application Owner, Classification, and Environment.

5. **Modify Driver Settings:** Review and customize Driver Configuration, Engine Control Values, and Global Configuration Values (GCVs), with priority on Driver Parameters that control input/output file format.

6. **Deploy to Identity Vault:** Deploy the driver, define security equivalence (typically using Admin or a DriversUser with Browse and Read rights), and exclude administrative roles from synchronization.

Key considerations include ensuring the Managed System Gateway driver is version 4.0.0.6 or higher for entitlements functionality and properly securing the driver with appropriate Identity Vault rights.

instruction: Which Identity Manager integration module includes the Delimited Text driver?
output: The Delimited Text driver is part of the Identity Manager Integration Module for Tools. This integration module includes three drivers: the Identity Manager driver for SOAP, the Identity Manager driver for REST, and the Identity Manager driver for Delimited Text.

instruction: Does the Delimited Text driver require separate activation from the base Identity Manager product?
output: Yes, the Delimited Text driver requires separate activation as part of the Identity Manager Integration Module for Tools. After purchasing this integration module, you will receive activation details in your NetIQ Customer Center.

instruction: What happens when you create a new Delimited Text driver in a driver set that already contains an activated driver from the Integration Module for Tools?
output: When you create a new Delimited Text driver in a driver set that already includes an activated driver from the Identity Manager Integration Module for Tools, the new Delimited Text driver automatically inherits the activation from the driver set. No additional activation is required.

instruction: How long does the Delimited Text driver run in evaluation mode if created in an unactivated driver set?
output: If you create the Delimited Text driver in a driver set that has not been previously activated with the Identity Manager Integration Module for Tools, the driver will run in evaluation mode for 90 days. You must activate the driver with this integration module during the evaluation period; otherwise, the driver will be disabled.

instruction: What happens if the Delimited Text driver activation has expired, and where can I find activation information?
output: If the Delimited Text driver activation has expired, the trace displays an error message indicating that you need to reactivate the driver to use it. For information on activation, refer to the 'Activating Identity Manager' section in the NetIQ Identity Manager Overview and Planning Guide.

instruction: Summarize the activation requirements for the Delimited Text driver.
output: The Delimited Text driver is part of the Identity Manager Integration Module for Tools, which requires separate activation after purchase. If created in a driver set with an already-activated driver from this module, the new Delimited Text driver inherits the activation. Otherwise, it runs in evaluation mode for 90 days and must be activated during this period to avoid being disabled. Activation details are provided through the NetIQ Customer Center after purchasing the integration module.

instruction: Why would you add packages to an existing Delimited Text driver?
output: You can add packages to an existing Delimited Text driver to add new functionality to it. This allows you to extend the capabilities of the driver without having to recreate it from scratch.

instruction: How do you add new packages to an existing Delimited Text driver in iManager?
output:
To add new packages to an existing Delimited Text driver:
1. Right-click the driver, then click Properties.
2. Click Packages, then upgrade the already installed Delimited Text Base package by selecting it, clicking the Select Operation cell, choosing Upgrade from the drop-down list, clicking Apply, and clicking OK to close the Package Management page.
3. Click the Add Packages icon.
4. Select the packages to install.
5. (Optional) If you want to see all available packages for the driver, clear the Show only applicable package versions option, then click OK.
6. Click Apply to install all of the packages listed with the Install operation.
7. (Conditional) Fill in the fields with appropriate information to install the package you selected for the driver, then click Next.
8. Read the summary of the installation, then click Finish.
9. Click OK to close the Package Management page after you have reviewed the installed packages.
10. Modify the driver configuration settings.
11. Deploy the driver.
12. Start the driver.
13. Repeat the process for each driver where you want to add the new packages.

instruction: How do you upgrade the Delimited Text Base package before adding new packages?
output:

instruction: Why would you need to set up one-way synchronization in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, you would set up one-way synchronization when your data synchronization needs to go only in one direction—either from the identity vault to the connected system (Publisher channel only) or from the connected system to the identity vault (Subscriber channel only). This requires disabling the channel that you don't use by clearing its filters and removing the associated file path configuration.

instruction: How do you configure one-way synchronization using only the Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver?
output:

1. In the Filter editor in Identity Console, clear the filters on the Subscriber channel:
   a. Select the object class (for example, the User class)
   b. Select 'Ignore' in the Subscribe section
   The Subscriber channel icon for the class changes to show that the class is no longer being synchronized.

2. Click Save to save the changes.

3. Edit the driver properties to remove the path specified for the Output File Path. This setting is located under the Subscriber Settings for the Driver Parameters on the Configuration tab.

instruction: How do you configure one-way synchronization using only the Subscriber channel in the Delimited Text driver?
output: To configure the Delimited Text driver for Subscriber-only synchronization, you need to clear the filters on the Publisher object and remove the path specified for the Input File Path in the Driver Parameters section. This disables the Publisher channel while keeping the Subscriber channel active.

instruction: Which driver parameter must be cleared when disabling the Subscriber channel in the Delimited Text driver?
output: When disabling the Subscriber channel in the Delimited Text driver, you must clear the Output File Path parameter. This setting is located under the Subscriber Settings for the Driver Parameters on the Configuration tab.

instruction: Which driver parameter must be cleared when disabling the Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver?
output: When disabling the Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver, you must clear the Input File Path parameter in the Driver Parameters section.

instruction: What happens to the channel icon when you set a class to 'Ignore' in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, when you select 'Ignore' in the Subscribe section for a class (such as the User class), the Subscriber channel icon for that class changes to visually indicate that the class is no longer being synchronized through the Subscriber channel.

instruction: Summarize the key steps for setting up one-way synchronization in the Delimited Text driver.
output: To set up one-way synchronization in the Delimited Text driver, you must disable the unused channel by: (1) clearing the filters on the channel you don't need by setting object classes to 'Ignore' in the Filter editor, and (2) removing the corresponding file path—either the Output File Path for Subscriber channel or the Input File Path for Publisher channel—from the Driver Parameters configuration. For Publisher-only synchronization, disable the Subscriber channel; for Subscriber-only synchronization, disable the Publisher channel.

instruction: What is the primary purpose of using style sheets in the Delimited Text driver for Identity Manager?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, style sheets are used to configure data synchronization and do most of the work in managing shared data. The driver passes text-based files largely unchanged to the style sheets, which perform the actual data transformation. Style sheets allow the Delimited Text driver to work with almost any text-based file that contains predictably repeatable patterns, making the driver flexible and customizable.

instruction: What is the <delimited-text> XML element in the Delimited Text driver?
output: The <delimited-text> XML element is the basis for data exchange in the Delimited Text driver. It serves as a structured XML representation of the data from text files. This element contains <record> elements, each with multiple <field> elements that have 'name' attributes and values. Style sheets convert text file contents into <delimited-text> elements for processing by Identity Manager.

instruction: Why does the Delimited Text driver rely heavily on style sheets rather than built-in parsing?
output: The Delimited Text driver relies heavily on style sheets because the driver is designed to be as flexible as possible. By passing text-based files largely unchanged to style sheets and letting the style sheets do most of the work, you can write new style sheets to allow the driver to work with almost any text-based file that contains predictably repeatable patterns. This design approach maximizes flexibility without requiring changes to the driver itself.

instruction: How do you design a Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver to read information from a text file?

The style sheet transforms the raw text data into the structured <delimited-text> format with <record> and <field> elements that Identity Manager can process.

instruction: Summarize the key concepts for configuring data synchronization using style sheets in the Delimited Text driver.

instruction: What Java interfaces does the Delimited Text driver provide to customize file processing?
output: The Delimited Text driver provides four Java interfaces to customize file processing: InputSorter, InputSource, PreProcessor, and PostProcessor. These interfaces enable you to add optional extensions to directly modify the driver's behavior when modifications cannot be made from a style sheet or DirXML Script.

instruction: What is the purpose of the InputSorter interface in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the InputSorter interface is used during the publish process to define the processing order of multiple input files. By default, the system where the driver is installed determines the processing order (for example, files on an NT system are processed in alphabetical order). You can use the InputSorter to impose a custom processing order that you require.

instruction: How does the InputSource interface customize the publish process in the Delimited Text driver?
output: The InputSource interface in the Delimited Text driver provides data from sources other than the files in the default location for the driver to process. For example, you can use this interface to check an FTP server for input files and then transfer the files to the local file system for processing by the driver.

instruction: What does the PreProcessor interface do in the Delimited Text driver's publish process?
output: The PreProcessor interface in the Delimited Text driver ties data manipulation required to prepare input files for driver processing directly to the driver. Before this interface was available, preprocessing was independent of the driver. Instead of creating a separate application that monitored another directory for input files, modified them, and then copied them to the driver's input directory, you can implement a PreProcessor class to do this preprocessing more directly.

instruction: What is the purpose of the PostProcessor interface in the Delimited Text driver?
output: The PostProcessor interface in the Delimited Text driver is used during the subscribe process to tie data manipulation required by the application consuming Identity Vault output directly to the driver. This allows you to process output data from the Identity Vault before it reaches the consuming application.

instruction: Are the Java interface extensions mandatory for the Delimited Text driver to function?
output: No, the Java interface extensions are optional in the Delimited Text driver. The driver continues to function as before without extensions. However, if you want to directly modify the behavior of the driver but have been unable to make these modifications from a style sheet or DirXML Script, extending the Delimited Text driver with these interfaces can be useful.

instruction: What are the high-level steps to implement custom Java functionality in the Delimited Text driver?
output: To implement custom Java functionality in the Delimited Text driver, you need to complete three processes: 1) Creating a Java Class that implements one or more of the provided interfaces (InputSorter, InputSource, PreProcessor, or PostProcessor), 2) Creating a Java .jar File from your compiled class, and 3) Configuring the Driver to Use the New Class so it is loaded and executed during driver operations.

instruction: Provide a summary of how the Delimited Text driver can be customized using Java interfaces.
output: The Delimited Text driver supports customization through four optional Java interfaces: InputSorter (to define processing order of multiple input files during publish), InputSource (to provide data from alternative sources during publish), PreProcessor (to prepare input files directly before driver processing during publish), and PostProcessor (to manipulate Identity Vault output during subscribe). These interfaces enable direct modification of driver behavior when style sheets or DirXML Script are insufficient. Implementation requires creating a Java class, packaging it as a .jar file, and configuring the driver to use the new class.

instruction: Which processes and interfaces are used during publish versus subscribe in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the publish process uses three interfaces: InputSorter (for defining processing order), InputSource (for providing alternative data sources), and PreProcessor (for preparing input files). The subscribe process uses one interface: PostProcessor (for manipulating Identity Vault output before it reaches the consuming application).

instruction: How do you configure the Delimited Text driver to use a new custom class after placing the .jar file?
output:
To configure the Delimited Text driver to use a new custom class:

1. In Identity Console, navigate to the Identity Manager Administration page by clicking IDM Administration in the Identity Manager frame.
2. Select the driver set containing the driver and click the driver icon.
3. Select the Configuration tab.
4. Click the Driver Parameters drop down, then click Edit XML.
5. Locate the <publisher-options> section for Publisher channel classes or the <subscriber-options> section for Subscriber channel classes.
6. Add the appropriate XML definition entries for your custom class based on its interface type (InputSorter, InputSource, PreProcessor, or PostProcessor).
7. Replace placeholder values with your actual class name (including full package identifier) and any required initialization parameters.
8. Click OK to save the configuration.

instruction: What XML configuration entry should be added to the Delimited Text driver for a custom InputSorter class?
output:
For a custom InputSorter class in the Delimited Text driver, add the following entry to the <publisher-options> section:

```xml
<definition display-name="InputSorter Class" name="input-sorter" type="string">
<value>com.acme.MyNewClass</value>
</definition>

<definition display-name="InputSorter init string" name="input-sorter-params" type="string">
<value>MY CONFIG PARAMS</value>
</definition>
```

Replace 'com.acme.MyNewClass' with your actual class name and full package identifier, and replace 'MY CONFIG PARAMS' with any initialization parameters needed by your class's init method. If no configuration parameters are required, you can omit the init string element entirely, and null will be passed to the init method.

instruction: What XML configuration is required in the Delimited Text driver for a custom InputSource class?

```

Replace 'com.acme.MyNewClass' with your full class name including package identifier. Replace 'MY CONFIG PARAMS' with configuration parameters to be passed to the init method. If no parameters are needed, omit the init string element and null will be passed to the init method.

instruction: How do you configure a PreProcessor class in the Delimited Text driver's XML configuration?

To configure a PreProcessor class in the Delimited Text driver, add this entry to the <publisher-options> section:

</definition>
```

Replace 'com.acme.MyNewClass' with your class name and full package identifier. Replace 'MY CONFIG PARAMS' with any initialization parameters your class requires. The init method of your class is responsible for parsing this configuration string. If no configuration is needed, you can leave off the init string element entirely, resulting in null being passed to the init method.

instruction: What is the XML configuration for a PostProcessor class in the Delimited Text driver?

Replace 'com.acme.MyNewClass' with your class name including full package information. Replace 'MY CONFIG PARAMS' with any initialization information to pass to the init method. Your class's init method must parse this configuration string. If no configuration string is needed, omit the entire parameters element, and null will be passed to the init method.

instruction: What is the purpose of modifying the publisher-options section in the Delimited Text driver configuration?
output: The <publisher-options> section in the Delimited Text driver configuration defines which parameters and values appear in the Driver Parameters section of the Driver Configuration page. When you add entries for custom classes (InputSorter, InputSource, or PreProcessor) to this section, the new options become visible in the interface. Each class you create that works on the Publisher channel requires an additional option entry in the <publisher-options> section. After updating this file, your new custom class options will be displayed and accessible through the driver's configuration interface.

instruction: In the Delimited Text driver, which custom class types are configured in the publisher-options section versus the subscriber-options section?
output:
In the Delimited Text driver configuration:

- The <publisher-options> section is used for custom classes that work on the Publisher channel: InputSorter, InputSource, and PreProcessor classes.

- The <subscriber-options> section is used for custom classes that work on the Subscriber channel: PostProcessor classes.

This separation reflects the different data flow directions in Identity Manager—Publisher channel handles events flowing from the connected system to the Identity Vault, while Subscriber channel handles events flowing from the Identity Vault to the connected system.

instruction: Where do you navigate in Identity Console to edit the XML configuration for custom classes in the Delimited Text driver?

instruction: What happens to the initialization parameters string configured for a custom class in the Delimited Text driver?
output: In the Delimited Text driver, the initialization parameters string configured for a custom class (specified in the *-params definitions like input-sorter-params, pre-processor-params, or post-processor-params) is passed to the init method of your custom class. Your class's init method is then responsible for parsing the information contained in this string. If your class doesn't require a configuration string, you can omit the entire init string element from the XML configuration, in which case null will be passed to the init method instead. This allows flexible initialization configuration for custom classes without requiring code changes.

instruction: Summarize the process of configuring custom classes in the Delimited Text driver after the .jar file has been deployed.
output: After deploying a custom class .jar file for the Delimited Text driver, you must update the driver's XML configuration through the Identity Console. Navigate to the driver's Configuration tab, access Driver Parameters, and click Edit XML. For Publisher channel classes (InputSorter, InputSource, PreProcessor), add definition entries to the <publisher-options> section; for Subscriber channel classes (PostProcessor), add entries to the <subscriber-options> section. Each definition specifies the fully-qualified class name and optional initialization parameters. The class name must include the complete package identifier, and initialization parameters are passed to the class's init method for parsing. If no parameters are needed, the init string element can be omitted. After adding the appropriate XML definitions and saving, the custom class options appear in the Driver Parameters interface and become active in the driver configuration.
